segments.arabic: [446] حدثنا سليمان بن حرب قال: حدثنا حماد بن زيد عن ثابت عن أبي رافع عن أبي هريرة
segments.english: Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Thabit, from Abu Rafi‘, from Abu Hurayrah:

segments.arabic: أن رجلا أسود أو امرأة سوداء كان يقم المسجد فمات فسأل النبي ﷺ عنه فقالوا مات قال أفلا كنتم آذنتموني به دلوني على قبره أو قال قبرها فأتى قبرها فصلى عليها
segments.english: A black man, or a black woman, used to sweep the mosque. He died, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, asked about him. They said: “He died.” He said: “Why did you not inform me about him? Show me his grave”—or he said, “her grave.” He came to her grave and prayed over her.

notes: The complete man-or-woman uncertainty remains. The selected masculine pronouns through his grave and the subsequent or he said her grave and feminine closing are retained, rather than harmonized to one gender. The historical print ends with feminine pronouns, as does the selected text; the modern print ends with masculine pronouns. Neither difference is silently corrected. Both English comparisons abbreviate the full Arabic chain.

segments.arabic: [447] حدثنا عبدان عن أبي حمزة عن الأعمش عن مسلم عن مسروق عن عائشة قالت
segments.english: ‘Abdan related to us, from Abu Hamzah, from al-A‘mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

segments.arabic: لما أنزلت الآيات من سورة البقرة في الربا خرج النبي ﷺ إلى المسجد فقرأهن على الناس ثم حرم تجارة الخمر
segments.english: When the verses from Surat al-Baqarah concerning usury were revealed, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to the mosque and recited them to the people. Then he prohibited trading in wine.

notes: The full chain and the sequence of revelation, recitation in the mosque and prohibition of wine trading remain. Usury provisionally renders الربا. The as well wording in the Bewley comparison is not added to the selected report. No contemporary ruling or additional Quranic verse text is inserted.

segments.arabic: [448] حدثنا أحمد بن واقد قال: حدثنا حماد عن ثابت عن أبي رافع عن أبي هريرة
segments.english: Ahmad ibn Waqid related to us. He said: Hammad related to us, from Thabit, from Abu Rafi‘, from Abu Hurayrah:

segments.arabic: أن امرأة أو رجلا كانت تقم المسجد
segments.english: A woman, or a man, used to sweep the mosque.

segments.arabic: ولا أراه إلا امرأة
segments.english: I do not think it was anyone but a woman.

segments.arabic: فذكر حديث النبي ﷺ أنه صلى على قبره
segments.english: Then he mentioned the account of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he prayed at his grave.

notes: This is the complete selected abbreviated report. The unnamed first-person uncertainty and the closing mention that the Prophet prayed at his grave remain as visible transmission notes in source order. The longer account at 446 is not copied into it. The selected final masculine pronoun agrees with both inspected prints; the Bewley comparison uses her grave.

The pinned Khan-family comparison is literally labelled 1.8.450f. Its body stops after mentioning the Hadith of the Prophet and omits the selected final grave-prayer clause. That omission is documented; this comparison is not evidence for the omitted words. The complete closing clause was checked in both Arabic prints and Bewley. The lower-case suffix is preserved as part of the reference.

segments.arabic: [449] حدثنا إسحاق بن إبراهيم قال: أخبرنا روح ومحمد بن جعفر عن شعبة عن محمد بن زياد عن أبي هريرة عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Rawh and Muhammad ibn Ja‘far informed us, from Shu‘bah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: إن عفريتا من الجن تفلت علي البارحة
segments.english: “An ifrit from the jinn suddenly came upon me last night”—

segments.arabic: أو كلمة نحوها
segments.english: or words like that—

segments.arabic: ليقطع علي الصلاة فأمكنني الله منه فأردت أن أربطه إلى سارية من سواري المسجد حتى تصبحوا وتنظروا إليه كلكم فذكرت قول أخي سليمان { رب اغفر لي وهب لي ملكا لا ينبغي لأحد من بعدي }
segments.english: “to interrupt my prayer. Allah gave me power over him, and I wanted to tie him to one of the pillars of the mosque so that, when morning came, all of you could look at him. Then I remembered the saying of my brother Sulayman: ‘My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that will not belong to anyone after me.’”

segments.arabic: قال روح فرده خاسئا
segments.english: Rawh said: He sent him away in disgrace.

notes: Both opening transmitters, the embedded or words like that uncertainty and the closing Rawh statement remain. The full selected Quranic quotation includes My Lord, forgive me; that clause is absent from the Bewley quotation but present in the Arabic prints and the individually matched Khan-family 1.8.450m body.

The historical print explicitly adds Allah in the final Rawh statement, while the selected text and modern print leave the subject as a pronoun. The working English retains He without inserting a named subject. Ifrit remains a transliterated source term. No larger account, additional Quranic phrase or explanatory parenthesis is imported.

segments.arabic: [450] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: حدثنا الليث قال: حدثنا سعيد بن أبي سعيد سمع أبا هريرة قال
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us. He said: Sa‘id ibn Abi Sa‘id related to us. He heard Abu Hurayrah say:

segments.arabic: بعث النبي ﷺ خيلا قبل نجد فجاءت برجل من بني حنيفة يقال له ثمامة بن آثال فربطوه بسارية من سواري المسجد فخرج إليه النبي ﷺ، فقال أطلقوا ثمامة فانطلق إلى نخل قريب من المسجد فاغتسل ثم دخل المسجد، فقال أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا رسول الله
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent horsemen toward Najd. They brought a man from Banu Hanifah called Thumamah ibn Uthal and tied him to one of the pillars of the mosque. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out to him and said: “Release Thumamah.” He went to some palm trees near the mosque and washed himself. Then he entered the mosque and said: “I testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.”

notes: The explicit he heard Abu Hurayrah link remains without inventing another said. The complete release, washing, return and testimony remain. The selected Arabic name آثال is retained unchanged; both inspected prints use أثال, and the Uthal transliteration follows the individually checked English comparisons. This spelling difference remains an independent-review item.

The selected body does not supply the later explanation he embraced Islam, a garden enclosure or an expanded testimony from the Khan-family comparison. The Shurayh chapter quotation remains separate Arabic browsing material and is not part of this narration.

segments.arabic: [451] حدثنا زكريا بن يحيى قال: حدثنا عبد الله بن نمير قال: حدثنا هشام عن أبيه عن عائشة قالت
segments.english: Zakariyya ibn Yahya related to us. He said: ‘Abd Allah ibn Numayr related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

segments.arabic: أصيب سعد يوم الخندق في الأكحل فضرب النبي ﷺ خيمة في المسجد ليعوده من قريب فلم يرعهم وفي المسجد خيمة من بني غفار إلا الدم يسيل إليهم فقالوا يا أهل الخيمة ما هذا الذي يأتينا من قبلكم فإذا سعد يغذو جرحه دما فمات فيها
segments.english: Sa‘d was wounded on the day of the Trench in the vein of his arm. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pitched a tent in the mosque so that he could visit him nearby. Nothing alarmed them—there was a tent of Banu Ghifar in the mosque—except blood flowing toward them. They said: “People of the tent, what is this coming to us from your direction?” There was Sa‘d, his wound streaming blood, and he died there.

notes: The selected unexpanded name Sa‘d, complete Banu Ghifar tent interruption, question and closing blood-flow statement remain. The selected يغذو and فيها agree with the modern print; the historical print has يغذ and منها. No silent Arabic normalization or variant replacement is made.

Vein of his arm provisionally renders الأكحل without a modern anatomical diagnosis. Al-Ayni explains the term as a vessel in the arm and يغذو as flowing; he records the final فيها as referring to the tent or the wound. The working English died there follows the tent reading, while the unresolved pronoun and the variant died from it remain documented. The personal name of the person who wounded him and other historical details from commentary are not inserted.

segments.arabic: [452] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن محمد بن عبد الرحمن بن نوفل عن عروة عن زينب بنت أبي سلمة عن أم سلمة قالت
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Nawfal, from ‘Urwah, from Zaynab bint Abi Salamah, from Umm Salamah, who said:

segments.arabic: شكوت إلى رسول الله ﷺ أني أشتكي قال طوفي من وراء الناس وأنت راكبة فطفت ورسول الله ﷺ يصلي إلى جنب البيت يقرأ بالطور وكتاب مسطور
segments.english: I complained to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that I was ill. He said: “Perform tawaf behind the people while riding.” I performed tawaf while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was praying beside the House, reciting: “By the Mount, and a book inscribed.”

notes: The complete chain through Zaynab bint Abi Salamah and Umm Salamah remains. Riding has no animal specified in this report; camel is not imported from the separate chapter quotation or the Bewley comparison. Both opening phrases of the recitation are retained, corresponding to Quran 52:1–2, instead of replacing them with a surah title alone. The selected House is not expanded inside the report.

segments.arabic: [453] حدثنا محمد بن المثنى قال: حدثنا معاذ بن هشام قال: حدثني أبي عن قتادة قال: حدثنا أنس
segments.english: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: Mu‘adh ibn Hisham related to us. He said: My father related to me, from Qatadah. He said: Anas related to us:

segments.arabic: أن رجلين من أصحاب النبي ﷺ خرجا من عند النبي ﷺ في ليلة مظلمة ومعهما مثل المصباحين يضيئان بين أيديهما فلما افترقا صار مع كل واحد منهما واحد حتى أتى أهله
segments.english: Two men among the companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, left the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on a dark night. With them were what looked like two lamps, shining before them. When they parted, one went with each of them until he reached his family.

notes: This is a distinct complete numbered report with its own full Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna chain. The original two leading newlines are accounted for separately by the existing reviewed layout map; they do not join this narration to 452. Both inspected prints introduce an untitled chapter 79 here, absent from the selected digital source. The selected chapter grouping is retained and the missing printed heading is disclosed; no thematic title is invented.

The historical print names one companion and tentatively identifies the other. Those names are absent from the selected text and modern print and are not inserted. The two Prophet honorifics, two lamps comparison, separation and each man reaching his family remain. The English EPUB’s explanatory miracle wording and Bewley’s separate identifying note are not made part of the selected narration.
